phenotype_specificity.statement: Each carrier is listed in Table S1 under a CD18-defined LAD1 class from neutrophil flow cytometry, with early-onset infections (see cases). No testing of other genes or exclusion of other causes is reported per person.

| LAD1<sup>o</sup> | P73 | ♀ | 0.23 | 4 | No | Omphalitis, otitis media, culture proven sepsis | No | Yes | *Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa* | 44940 | Expired |

Based on the CD18 expression on neutrophils, LAD1 was sub-classified into three phenotypes viz. severe (LAD1°) with CD18 expression <2% moderate (LAD1^-) phenotype with CD18 expression 2%–30%, and mild (LAD1^+) phenotype with CD18 expression ≥30%.
Umbilical cord related complications like omphalitis (64%) and delayed separation (62%) were the most common manifestation seen in the LAD1° and LAD1^- cases.

functional.statement: No assay of the variant itself. Patient-cell evidence only: carriers were assigned a CD18-expression class by neutrophil flow cytometry (Table S1 'Phenotype' column; class definitions quoted). Per-person CD18 percentages are not given in the text.

As a part of the diagnostic workup of LAD the flow cytometric expression of CD18, CD11 markers on leukocytes was assessed.

Based on the CD18 expression on neutrophils, LAD1 was sub-classified into three phenotypes viz. severe (LAD1°) with CD18 expression <2% moderate (LAD1^-) phenotype with CD18 expression 2%–30%, and mild (LAD1^+) phenotype with CD18 expression ≥30%.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Intronic variant at the canonical splice acceptor (-1) of intron 6 (batch HGVS c.742-1G>A; protein not predicted). Paper labels it 'IVS6-1', 'Splice site'. The paper describes LAD1 as caused by defects in ITGβ2 encoding CD18; cohort-level statement on VWFA-domain variants and absent CD18 expression quoted.

quotes.quote: | | VWFA | c.742-1G\>A | IVS6-1 | Intron 6 | Splice site | P60,P61, P73# | Novel |
LAD1 is caused due to defect in the ITGβ2 gene encoding the common beta subunit of β2 integrins (CD18) (5–9).
Out of the total mutations identified in the VWFA domain, 89% of them resulted in absent expression of CD18 on PMNs causing severe infection in LAD1° and LAD1^- cases.

computational_predictions.statement: No per-variant score is given in the text. Figure 1C is said to plot CADD and MAF for novel variants via PopViz; the figure is not available as text.

quotes.quote: Combined annotation–dependent depletion (CADD) and Minor allele frequency (MAF) scores of the variants reported in gnomAD and novel variants identified in our cohort for the genes (C)

authors_classification.statement: No per-variant classification. The authors describe all 57 ITGβ2 variants in Table S2 collectively as 'disease-causing'; Table S2's reference column for this variant is quoted under variant.as_written_in_papers.

quotes.quote: Direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGβ2 gene revealed 57 disease-causing variants in 105 patients (Table S2), including 30 patients we have previously reported (18).

concerns: Zygosity comes from the Table S2 convention: only '#' (heterozygous) is defined, so carriers without '#' are taken as homozygous; the paper does not say so per person and reports no parental testing.
Supplementary Table S1 in the converted text is truncated at 60,000 of 123,896 characters; the rows used here are present, but any later columns or notes may be missing.
The paper includes 30 patients previously reported by the same group (ref 18, PMID 25703682) without naming them; carriers here may also appear in that paper.
Table S1 column 'Umbilical Cord Separation' is Yes/No and does not say whether 'Yes' means delayed separation.
Transcript is not stated in the paper; HGVS as given is assumed to be on the batch transcript NM_000211.5.
P73 carries a second ITGB2 variant, c.751G>A (p.Gly251Ser), also marked heterozygous; the two '#' marks are the only evidence of compound heterozygosity, and phase was not shown.
P60 and P61 carry the same variant; both are from consanguineous families with family history 'No'. The paper does not say whether they are related (127 cases came from 125 families).
Table S2 labels this variant 'Novel' in its reference column.
notes_for_panel: Three carriers in one multicentre Indian cohort: P60 and P61 (no '#', implied homozygous) and P73 (heterozygous, with c.751G>A p.Gly251Ser as the other '#' variant). Clinical data are one Table S1 row each; P60 and P61 were lost to follow up, P73 died.
